home.headline: It began in a Discord chat where I was learning English
home.designNote: The idea came out of learning English on Discord. Talking with people there late into the evening, I kept running into small moments worth holding on to — and nowhere to put them. So I built this place: an open invitation to the friends I met in those chats to sign in with their own account and write down what we came across. One stream, newest first. Like a post, leave a comment, and see what everyone else noticed.

about.title: About Encounter
about.intro: A site that does one thing: writes meetings down. It does not ask for completeness, and it does not ask you to keep going — just a line whenever you remember someone, pass somewhere, or finish a book.
about.dataIntro: Everything lives in the PostgreSQL database behind {envVar} — there is no second copy.
about.dataEmptyBody: — the site still opens, but the stream is empty and nothing can be saved.
about.dataLiveBody: — you can post, react, comment, edit and delete right here, and every entry belongs to whoever wrote it.
about.deployStep1: Push the repository to GitHub and import it in Vercel. The framework is detected as Next.js automatically.
about.deployStep2: In the Vercel project open Storage → Create Database → Postgres. The connection string is injected as {envVar} for you.
about.deployStep3: Put the same connection string in your local .env file, then run {init} to create the tables.
about.deployStep4: Redeploy once and you can write entries in production.
about.stackBody: Next.js App Router with Server Components and Server Actions, Tailwind CSS, next-intl for English and Chinese, and PostgreSQL through the Neon serverless driver. Everything runs on Vercel — no extra backend, no client-side state library.
